stem: Which record correctly distinguishes a target from an observation?
choices: “Temperature 25 °C” because the target value can stand in for the room condition when the system is under control.
“Temperature 27 °C” because target and observation describe the same environmental variable.
“Room hot” because location, unit, and time are secondary once an abnormal condition is recognized.
rationale: A target describes the intended condition; a measurement describes what was actually observed. Keeping those values separate preserves the difference between plan and reality and makes the record reconstructable. Including the sensor location and time also helps later reviewers understand whether the measurement is representative and when the deviation occurred.
